docs(coord): red-team of the coordination bus Answers the redteam/matrix task assigned on 06/11: publishing with gh, without MCP and without a session, the fleet accepts the claim as a real agent (it shows up in coord_read with lane and scope) and the collision detector trusts it, so a spoofed claim blocks the legitimate owner of that scope for the claim TTL. The inbox is closed: coord_pending resolves identity from the caller and ignores the payload, so neither a forged agent nor a foreign session id reaches another agent's inbox. That means no prompt injection through the bus, only a denial of service on the coordination layer. Mitigations ranked by cost: require validated identity in the collision detector (the rule the inbox already uses), take the publisher identity from the GitHub author instead of the payload, sign the payload per agent, and refuse claims outside the caller's lane in the post tool.

docs(vpnsec): coord_http exposure measured and the auth that fits the tailnet Answers the vpnsec task assigned on 06/11. Measured from this host: the MCP on 100.121.100.103:8765 completes the initialize handshake and serves tools/list (8051 bytes of schemas) with no authentication at all; Basic by header changes nothing because FastMCP drops the Authorization header before the tools. The server binds only the tailnet IP and the NixOS firewall config does not list 8765 on tailscale0, but the live nftables ruleset was not readable from my shell, so the network barrier is not confirmed here. Risk, combined with today's bus red-team: an outsider with reach can paralyse lanes (a spoofed claim blocks the legitimate owner) and fake agents in the board; prompt injection into another agent's inbox does not work, because the inbox resolves identity from the caller. Proposal: bearer token via RemoteAuthProvider, one token per agent stored as a hash in the roster, with the shared-secret middleware as the immediate stopgap, the Tailscale ACL as defence in depth, and the post tool binding the claim to the caller's lane so the spoofing path closes with it.

feat(voice): the speaker separability measurement, with the wakeword verdict The decisive measurement, reproduced with the WeSpeaker backend actually running (the runtime was fixed by the sweep: torchaudio in the devShell plus the package from the lab venv): intra-speaker cosine n=34, mean 0.3526, p95 0.6435, against inter-speaker n=102, mean 0.3196, p95 0.5751, with an inter maximum of 0.8379. The distributions touch, so the enrollment gate does not hold: the owner's own noisy takes fall below the 0.82 threshold that the gate uses, and a false positive above the threshold is possible. The honest answer to the pending voice item is therefore the wakeword, not more machine learning. The tool ships with the sweep's fix (it tries the runtime importable in the current environment first and only falls back to the lab venv, whose torchaudio without a matching torch broke the previous run), and the audit records the enrollment that exists (8 samples, consistency min 0.8552, mean 0.9015, verify 0.9006) together with the numbers that close the question.

docs(voice): the wakeword gate design, reusing the openWakeWord model we already declare The text gate is measured (recall 0.923, F1 0.889) and the speaker route is measured to fail: with WeSpeaker actually running, intra-speaker cosine p95 0.6435 against inter-speaker p95 0.5751 and max 0.8379, so the distributions touch and the 0.82 threshold would reject the owner's own noisy takes while still allowing a false positive. The wakeword is the signal that separates the TV from the owner with confidence, because it is an acoustic pattern the TV never produces and it does not depend on the speaker. The house already has what is needed: models.nix declares openwakeword with the hey_jarvis, embedding and melspectrogram models (pinned, nothing to download), and the asrd already carries per-segment signals (spk, voices, wav) where a wake state fits without touching the rest of the path. The existing wakeword daemon is a desktop hotkey service (graphical-session target, DISPLAY/WAYLAND) and does not serve the voice pipeline. The design has three steps (wake state on the microphone stream, one more per-segment field, the candidate rule in the gate module), the honest UX cost (the owner says hey jarvis, or the cheaper variant where the wakeword is only a negative filter for the TV), and the measurement that comes first: run openWakeWord offline over the 259 segments in logs/audio and publish the recall on the owner's segments, the false positives on the TV ones and the threshold curve. Nothing was applied: no flags, no services, no change in duplex-voice.py (that wiring belongs to the lane that owns the duplex).

feat(voice): measure the house wakeword scorer over the voice corpus Reuses the house scorer (modules/ai/ww_scorer.py: mel + embedding + classifier straight from the pinned ONNX models) instead of a new stack, so the measurement needs no new package and no service change. First pass over 60 segments of logs/audio: the score distribution is min 0.0001, p50 0.0016, p90 0.014 and max 0.9301, and exactly one segment fires above 0.3 (and above 0.9) — the one the duplex log shows as a 'respond' segment, i.e. the true wake. So on this corpus the wakeword is precise: the ambient and TV segments sit three orders of magnitude below the threshold. The full corpus run is in flight; the tool also exposes the scorer's own calibration mode (--positive-dir/--negative-dir/--target-fpr) for choosing the threshold on labelled folders.

feat(voice): measure the house voice pipeline and fix the ASRD subprocess environment The trigger bench posts the fixture straight to the whisper server, so the house chain (VAD, segmentation, anti_halluc gate) was never measured on it. scripts/voice-pipeline-probe.py drives the real duplex-asrd through the same stdio protocol the duplex uses, feeds the trigger fixtures in real time with digital silence at the end to close the segment, pairs every clip with the same audio on the raw whisper path, and keeps a positive control (real speech wavs) so that no text cannot be confused with a broken probe. The sample is seeded per category, so two runs on the same slice are comparable. The ASRD environment resolver asked nix for nixpkgs#gcc.lib, a path that does not exist on the current nixpkgs (the attribute is gcc.cc.lib), and swallowed the failure: the resolver returned only zlib and the ASRD survived only because the parent environment already carried the gcc library path. On a restart from a clean environment that kills the ASRD before its ready line, which is exactly the 0/10 sem-segmento symptom. scripts/asrd_env.py resolves the attribute paths that exist, verifies the soname in the result, falls back to a store search when nix cannot answer, and reports what is missing; the ASRD now prints a JSON error instead of dying silently on the numpy import. Also measured (10 clips per category, 12 s window, reduplication): the raw whisper path hallucinates on 10 of 10 clips while the house pipeline returns text on 3 of 10, and the same slice reproduces exactly (3 of 10, 6 segments closed) across runs. The gate kills the segments with weak audio stats and lets the confident ones through.

docs(voice): the trigger bench measures the whisper server, not the house The number that was heading for the owner's decision sheet (0.925) comes from a bench that posts the fixture straight to whisper-server: it never runs the VAD, the segmentation or the anti_halluc gate, so it says what whisper does with the whole clip, not what the house would answer. Two of my own readings were wrong for the same reason and are corrected in the audit: the empty_ok column is not the VAD dropping clips (it is whisper returning empty text), and the house VAD threshold is fixed at 0.5 (the AdaptiveVAD class exists but its update_threshold is never called). The house pipeline was measured with the new probe (same audio, same 12 s window, paired comparison, positive control 5/5) over 123 distinct trigger clips: the raw whisper path hallucinates on 83 of them (0.67) while the house chain delivers text on 3 (0.024), so the chain cuts 96 percent of the trigger hallucinations. The VAD never opens a segment for silence, nonspeech and music, and the gate kills what gets through; the residual is syllable repetition (3 of 40) with confident audio, which is what the wakeword would cover. docs(voice): the room level changes the VAD, not the residual The audit still carried a hypothesis ('in a real room the VAD may catch the TV') instead of a number, and with the threshold now known to be fixed at 0.5 the question became measurable. The probe gained a level sweep: the same clips scaled to a target RMS, 5 clips per category per level, 60 feeds in total, with the clipping measured (worst case 2.6 percent of the samples). Result: the raw whisper path hallucinates on music and repetition at every level (5 of 5 each) and the house chain delivered text on none of the 60 feeds. The level changes how many segments the VAD opens (repetition 7 to 3, music 5 to 2) and the gate closes all of them, so the residual is not a function of the room level: what leaks is the clip whose syllable pattern looks like speech, not the volume. Also corrects a claim of mine in the audit: I wrote that the live ASRD does not have the v6 gate. It does (v6 and v7 landed on 20/10 and the process started on 08/11); what it misses is the offline start fix of 09/11 and the environment fix, so the pending restart matters for the start, not for the gate. The tools index was regenerated with the house generator, which also picked up the voice tools that were never indexed.

fix(voice): close the measured repetition residual with a rule that can be switched off The residual of the house voice chain was three syllable-repetition clips ('Ah, ah, ah.', 'Tataataataata. Uh uh uh.', 'E E E E E'). The repetition rule the ASRD had only caught the hyphenated form ('A-a-a-a'), which none of them use, so it killed none. The cost was measured before the change, on 199 real transcripts from logs/audio transcribed by the house whisper server: a repeated-token rule kills 3 of the 3 survivors and 1 of 199 real utterances (0.5 percent; the one case is 'Nao, nao, nao, nao.'). The token rule is not conditioned on the audio because the hallucinated audio arrives confident (avg_logprob -0.24 to -0.43, above the -0.45 threshold), which is exactly why it costs 0.5 percent of real speech instead of zero. The rule now lives in one module (scripts/voice_text_rules.py, with tests), is used by the ASRD, and can be switched off from the environment (JARVIS_VOICE_REPEAT_RULE=0) without touching code. A/B on the same ten clips (the slice that leaked, reproduced by id with the new probe option --clip-ids): the raw whisper path hallucinates on 10 of 10 either way; with the rule on the house chain delivers 0 of 10, with it off 3 of 10. The residual measured earlier is therefore closed, at a measured cost of one real utterance in 199. Caveat recorded in the audit: the residual is noisy between runs (same slice gave 0, 3 and 1 of 10), because the GPU transcription is not deterministic and the segment cut moves with timing, so the rule's robust proof is the test (3 of 3 forms) plus the cost measurement, and the rule only reaches the live process on the pending restart.

The cost was measured before the change, on 199 real transcripts from logs/audio transcribed by the house whisper server: a repeated-token rule kills 3 of the 3 survivors and 1 of 199 real utterances (0.5 percent; the one case is 'Nao, nao, nao, nao.'). The token rule is not conditioned on the audio because the hallucinated audio arrives confident (avg_logprob -0.24 to -0.43, above the -0.45 threshold), which is exactly why it costs 0.5 percent of real speech instead of zero. The rule now lives in one module (scripts/voice_text_rules.py, with tests), is used by the ASRD, and can be switched off from the environment (JARVIS_VOICE_REPEAT_RULE=0) without touching code. A/B on the same ten clips (the slice that leaked, reproduced by id with the new probe option --clip-ids): the raw whisper path hallucinates on 10 of 10 either way; with the rule on the house chain delivers 0 of 10, with it off 3 of 10. The residual measured earlier is therefore closed, at a measured cost of one real utterance in 199. Caveat recorded in the audit: the residual is noisy between runs (same slice gave 0, 3 and 1 of 10), because the GPU transcription is not deterministic and the segment cut moves with timing, so the rule's robust proof is the test (3 of 3 forms) plus the cost measurement, and the rule only reaches the live process on the pending restart.

feat(voice): a tool to measure the cost of a voice gate rule in real speech

feat(voice): a tool to test whether any audio-side signal separates hallucination from real speech The audio arm of the voice gate uses no_speech_prob and avg_logprob, and both were measured useless on trigger hallucinations (they kill 0 of 111: the hallucinated transcript arrives confident, median no_speech_prob 0.000 and median avg_logprob between -0.22 and -0.30 against a -0.45 threshold). The whisper server exposes more that the gate ignores: per-word probability, the token ids (which give the compression ratio, one of Whisper's own heuristics) and the segment duration. This tool measures each candidate on both classes (real speech from logs/audio, trigger hallucinations from the bench JSONL) and reports the separation and the cost at the threshold that kills 90 percent of the hallucinations. The tool does not touch the gate: it is evidence for the voice lane to decide whether an audio arm is repairable at all, which is what arXiv 2606.23060 (Interspeech 2026) makes the open question.

docs(voice): the cost of the text rules on real speech, and the floor under them A text rule in the voice gate is not free, and that cost was never measured: the house had the gain (the gate real kills 87 of 111, residual 0.200) without the price. Measured on the 1817 real transcripts of logs/audio: 134 of them (7.4 percent) have their exact text in the lexicon ('Obrigado.', 'Tchau.', 'Muito bom.'), 34 start with 'e ai' (1.9 percent), and the candidate prefix rule kills 1 of 1817 (0.06 percent). That one is not a defect of the rule, it is the floor under any text gate: the same string ('E ai, o que e isso?') is in the real speech and in the hallucinations, and no function of the text separates the two classes. Which is also why the wakeword is not optional for the residual. The document also records what the 2026 literature says (arXiv 2606.23060: text metrics degrade without a reference transcript and the strong signal is probing the decoder internals, which whisper.cpp does not expose; arXiv 2609.32560 and 2501.11378: the VAD before the decoder is the primary defense, and the house already has it).

feat(tools): a checker that stops forbidden characters from leaving the house Two of my bus notes went out with a CJK character in the middle of the text, and the lesson written in memory did not hold it: what holds it is mechanical. scripts/check-text-chars.py blocks CJK, full-width forms, emoji and arrows and passes Portuguese accents and ordinary typography, with a usage contract and a non-zero exit so it can gate a script. The sweep's own note about the loop was right that publishing a convention is not enough; this is the same lesson applied to the text itself instead of to the decision to send.

feat(voice): the composed 'e ai' rule, with its cost measured first The sweep measured the candidate rule on 1817 real transcripts: 'e ai' at the start and the rest also looking like a hallucination (lexicon, hallucination greeting, repetition, 'legenda', or 'e ai' repeated three or more times). It kills one real utterance (0.06 percent, 'E ai, o que e isso?') and ten of the 24 gate survivors, and that cost is the floor of any text gate rather than a defect of the rule. The rule is conservative on purpose: 'E ai, tudo bom?' passes. It is now implemented in the voice lane with the same pattern as the repetition rule: one module with a test, an environment switch (JARVIS_VOICE_GREETING_RULE=0), and wired into the ASRD after the dry 'e ai' kill that already existed. Parity is proven: comparing this implementation with the measured one (measure-voice-rule-cost.py) over the 111 bench samples gives 111 of 111 identical verdicts, and both kill the same 10 of the 24 survivors. The gate residual on the whole clip therefore drops from 24 of 111 (0.216) to 14 of 111 (0.126). The decision sheet and the audit carry the rule, its cost, and how to switch it off.

docs(harness): the stale wake diagnosis, with the end of the loop proved The wakes that reached the sessions carried a state that did not exist on the machine receiving them: the local watcher journal shows the same queue events with the right time and without the [WATCHER hh:mm] prefix, the prefix itself was about fifty minutes ahead of the local clock, and one wake pointed the queue top at the era of 09/11 while the real queue had today's era on top. The only lane of the fleet that is not in the local roster and that posts on the bus is crouton-alpha (termux/vpnsec), which reads a stale copy of the queue and of the vault. That stale era is the one carrying the old gate number, which is why the lane kept repeating it for hours after the gate had been measured for real. The end of the loop is proved: the similarity dedupe already in main scores the repeated stale wakes between 0.77 and 0.87 of similarity, so once that machine syncs the clone the repetition stops being delivered. The action (git pull, and fix the clock with chrony or NTP) is published on the bus. A plugin filter for wakes with a clock ahead of the local one is proposed for the next rebuild, since a rebuild is the owner's call.

docs(gate): the new health endpoint is safe, and the session cap covers 69 percent of what the gate warns about The endpoint GET /__gate/health, new in the house, listens on 127.0.0.1:8095 only (the tailnet address refuses the connection), answers with counters and leaks no upstream URL, key or address. The path /health next to it is not local: it falls through to the forwarder, took 5.4 seconds in the measurement and relayed the upstream, so a probe with the wrong path looks like a dead service and still spends upstream quota. The fleet believed the two provider fixes were waiting for a rebuild, because the gate runs the store copy. Measured: the store copy already has both (small_bucket and ctx_short_circuit), the live process started after those commits, and the context guard has already short-circuited 176 requests locally. The pending rebuild does not include them. And the session cap is not a theoretical guard: of the 54 requests the gate warned about in 6 hours, 37 (69 percent) are above 1.05 MB, which is the 262144 token ceiling. The median warned request is 5.46 MB, about 1.37 million tokens, above the API ceiling itself.

fix(voice): the E2E battery read 0/10 because the ASRD dropped every short segment Three measured defects, in the live voice path: The stack was down, not waiting for a restart: the client and the ASRD die on the numpy import of the karaok venv when libstdc++ is not on LD_LIBRARY_PATH. The resolver asked nix for nixpkgs#gcc.lib, which does not exist on this nixpkgs (the attribute is gcc.cc.lib), and swallowed the failure, so the ASRD survived only because the inherited environment already carried the path. scripts/asrd_env.py now resolves the attribute paths that exist, verifies the soname in the result, falls back to the store and reports what is missing; duplex-voice-run.sh uses the same resolver for the client, which needs it too. The voice is up again. The ASRD dropped every short segment: seg_to_text returned a bare string for segments under 0.4 s while its caller unpacks a tuple, so the handler swallowed 'ValueError: not enough values to unpack (expected 2, got 0)' and the segment was lost. That was the cause of the 0/10 sem-segmento. The guard is now _min_segment, at module level, with a test. The injection list was never consumed: the same wav was re-fed every tick (the ASRD heard the phrase repeatedly and returned a hallucination) and the mic stayed muted for good after an injection. The list is consumed now and the whisper context is cleared, because the injected phrase is test material and was polarising the next transcription ('Jarvis, que horas sao?' became 'Servico que horas sao?'). Measured: the isolated injection now transcribes whole ('Qual a previsao do tempo de amanha?', 417 ms, and the saved segment carries the full audio, rms 5457 against 5555 of the source). Opt-in telemetry (JARVIS_ASR_TRACE=1) logs every ASRD line, including the empty ones, and the traceback when the ASRD raises, because 'sem-segmento' was opaque without it. Still open, honestly: the battery in series stays 0/10 because the first scenario lands on no-response (whisper turns 'Jarvis' into 'Servico' on the synthetic wav) and the following ones are injected while the client is still answering, so their segment misses the battery's 40 s window. The pipeline defect is fixed; what is left is the pacing of the test.

docs(voice): the house path now leaves one case, and it is a laugh The voice lane restarted the voice stack at 16:10 with the composed 'e ai' rule inside, so the blocker this lane had documented (the rebuild does not restart the voice stack) is gone and the house path could be measured against the code that runs. Measured with the pipeline probe, 20 clips per category: the raw inference path hallucinates 66 of 80, and the house path (VAD, segment, gate) delivers text on 1 of 80. The single survivor is 'Hahahaha', a laugh, which the deny list keeps on purpose because laughter is a social signal the owner wants the agent to use. The real speech control passed 3 of 3, so the house path does not kill real speech. That is the cleanest possible framing of the wakeword decision: what is left of the house path is speech that looks like speech, and the case is a laugh. No text rule can kill that laugh without killing the real laugh of whoever is speaking, which is exactly what the wakeword is for, and why its threshold cannot be guessed.

docs(voice): the last residual case is a laugh, and closing it is a product call The remediation with today's code leaves one case out of eighty trigger clips: 'Hahahaha', a laugh. The separated repetition rule in the ASRD does not catch it (there is no separator) and neither does the sweep's concatenated rule (the pattern is not three exact repetitions of one group). Measured on the 1817 real transcripts of the house with the new tool scripts/measure-repeat-rule-cost.py: a concatenated rule catches the case at zero measured cost (0 of 1817), while the rule in place today kills 15 of 1817 (0.83 percent). The number does not hide the trade-off: a laugh is a social signal the house keeps on purpose (SOCIAL_KEEP in duplex-asrd.py), so a concatenated rule also kills the owner's own laugh. The decision sheet therefore asks the owner to choose between closing the case mechanically and losing the laugh, or keeping the laugh and accepting that trigger. One correction of my own number in the same commit: I published the cost of the rule in place as one real utterance in 199 (0.5 percent). The sample was too small; on the whole corpus it is 15 in 1817 (0.83 percent), with cases like 'Nao, nao, nao.' and 'sim sim sim nao foi antes nao'. The direction of the decision is unchanged, but the smaller figure I published was not the number.

fix(voice): a half-written wav must not take the voice down The voice client died on 10/11 at 17:27:23 with wave.Error: file does not start with RIFF id: it opened a wav that was still being written (a burst of writes; the file was valid 0.9 seconds later with 44 kB and the RIFF magic). The exception was not handled on that path, so the whole process died, and the client's finally block then logged 'dormindo: LoRA off, wakeword de volta', which made the crash look like a planned sleep. This corrects my earlier reading that the voice had gone to sleep on purpose. The fix: _open_wav_safe validates the RIFF header, retries a few times (the file may be mid-write) and returns None instead of raising, with a log; the three unprotected call sites (AEC registration, voice enrollment and wav concatenation) now use it. A turn without audio cannot take the voice down. The tests cover a partial file, an empty file, a missing file and a valid one. The finally block already stopped reporting a false success on the wakeword handover. The voice was down since that crash and is up again with this code.

fix(voice): a failing tool must not take the voice down, and add the watchdog script Two pieces against the class of crash that silenced the voice on 10/11, since the client is avulso and the self-heal only watches units: a tool that raises now becomes an error string for the model (call_tool_safe) instead of climbing through call_tool into the main loop and killing the process, which was the exact path of the 17:27:23 crash; and scripts/voice-watchdog.sh checks whether the client and the ASRD are up and, with --restart, brings the stack back through the runner, which resolves the library path so the client does not die on the numpy import. The script installs nothing and changes no config; the missing piece is the owner pointing a timer at it. Tests cover a tool that raises, a tool that passes through, and that the main loop calls the wrapper.

docs(research): microtask platforms, UHRS, and how the house stack fits The owner asked for research on the microtask and AI-training platforms, and how the Laya and the local or API models, with the screen-reading MCP and the humanized input, could be used to earn, focused on quick microtasks, yes/no decisions and access to UHRS. The research: UHRS is Microsoft's Universal Human Relevance System, a relevance-judgment platform reached through Clickworker or Toloka, paying 7 to 14 dollars per active hour for qualified workers against 5 to 9 for image labeling; access needs a clickworker account, the English assessment, a dedicated LiveID and a qualification run of 50 to 100 test items, and the Clickworker support states that access is temporarily disabled when the login goes through a proxy or VPN, which is exactly this machine's vpnsec mode. The map covers Clickworker, OneForma, Toloka and Mindrift (15 to 30 per hour entry, 60 to 100+ for domain experts), Appen's CrowdGen (up to 100+ per hour for specialists), RWS TrainAI and LXT, Outlier, DataAnnotation, TELUS Digital, Datavio and friends, Microworkers and SproutGigs, Prolific and CloudResearch Connect (14 to 16.5 per hour in the examples, 10 average) and ySense, plus why MTurk is not to be counted on for a new Brazilian account. The plan has three rungs: triage the pipeline with the local models so only the tasks that pay are opened, use the local models to draft the label and the explanation while the human decides with human_input, and build the service the owner can actually sell, since the house already owns the stack these companies sell (voice interface, screen reading, humanized input, local and cloud models). The compliance line is explicit: automating clicks or answers breaks the terms, gets accounts banned and payments clawed back, so the model drafts and the human decides. The document ends with what the owner needs: the English test, a session with direct egress and no vpnsec, one or two platforms to qualify, and the first paying B2B customer.

feat(tools): the judgment bench that decides if Laya can answer by proxy The owner answered the compliance point: it will not answer alone, he will train the Laya model, so the answer is his, by proxy. That makes the fastest start obvious: do not start with the training, start with the training data that the platforms already demand. The decision and the order of attack are now in the research doc (addendum): today, twenty minutes for the clickworker account and the UHRS English test (free, direct egress, no vpnsec, because the access is disabled behind a proxy or VPN), which also delivers the first labels for free because the fifty to a hundred qualification items are exactly the dataset; in parallel, an application to Mindrift, whose approval is an application rather than an assessment chain. And in parallel, with nobody's approval needed, the concordance bench, so the training is not a leap in the dark: the number decides the mode (at or above 95 percent the model may answer alone, 85 to 95 it proposes and the owner confirms, below 85 there is no delegation), with the same method as the honest voice bench (a hand-written held-out, zero leakage) and a Wilson interval, so ninety-five percent on twenty items is not mistaken for certainty. What lands here: scripts/judgment-bench.py (reads the owner's dataset, measures agreement against the local router, prints the misses and the recommended mode; the self-test proves the mechanics without a model) and data/judgments/SCHEMA.md (the dataset format, how to collect the labels from the qualification items, how to train and measure, and what the dataset does not solve).

feat(renda): the owner's labels become a Laya dataset, in the format his pipeline already reads The last mile of the delegation is the training, and the house already has that pipeline: the mt5 repo carries the Laya dataset in the format {'type': 'choice', 'state': ..., 'question': ..., 'options': {...}, 'answer': ...} — and a relevance judgment is exactly a choice with four options (Highly, Moderately, Slightly, Not Relevant). So no new trainer is needed: scripts/judgment-dataset.py turns the owner's labels (the format of data/judgments/SCHEMA.md) plus the practice items into train/test/calib in that format, which the owner's existing pipeline consumes. The script refuses to let the held-out leak into the training (the owner's own held-out file is read separately and never enters the train split), and it warns when the class distribution is lopsided, because a model trained on one class learns a prior instead of the rubric. The twelve practice items are now a versioned file (data/judgments/uhrs-practice-items.jsonl) instead of living only inside the bench, so the bench and the dataset builder read the same source. The self-test earned its keep twice: it caught the calibration slice being taken from the same array as the training (leakage between train and calib) and the split not adapting to a small dataset, which left one training item. Both fixed; the self-test is green and the demo dataset comes out in the Laya format with the four options and the chosen level.

feat(renda): the screener, the pause, and the bench talking to a model that answers Three things the owner asked for, all measured and tested. The screener (scripts/task-screener.py) triages the panel: the costly part of microtask work is opening fifteen tabs to find out that twelve do not pay. It parses the listing (payment per hour or per task, real duration, number of tasks, format, English requirement), computes the effective rate and then the rate adjusted by motor effort (clicking and typing 1.0, reading and judging 1.6, image 1.8, writing 3.0), because the owner is a disabled person and the effort per click is what decides the value per hour. Above US$ 12/h it is worth it, below US$ 4/h it is not, and the borderline cases go to the local model with a rubric. The platform rates are the ones measured in the 13/11 research. The self-test caught that a listing in Portuguese ('US$ 0,50 por tarefa') did not match the pattern and that the model was being asked for by a name the server does not carry. The watchdog now respects the pause (scripts/voice-watchdog.sh): --pause writes the voice pause flag and drops the stack, --resume lifts it, and the house pause flag (the one the nightwatch uses) pauses the voice too. Paused, the watchdog says so and starts nothing, so a deliberate stop is not undone by the next timer tick. The self-test proves the three cases against a temporary state directory, without touching the real state. The bench was calling a model that could not answer: the router announces bonsai but cannot load it (HTTP 500, VRAM), while the duplex 4B on :8092 answers fine. Both the bench and the screener now discover and test which server answers, and the bench's prompt presents the four rubric options instead of asking for the owner's own string. With that, the bench measures for real: 7 of 12 (58.3 percent) against the base 4B with no fine-tune, and the per-level F1 shows it collapses onto '3' (level 2 and level 1 at F1 0.00), which is exactly what the training on the owner's labels has to fix. Also recorded: the owner's decision on the default model and the VRAM measurement behind it (the router is down because the bonsai does not fit; one instance of the 4B MTP closes both).

feat(skills): import the three Anthropic skills that do not duplicate the house, tested The Anthropic skills (194k stars) have the SAME frontmatter the house uses (name, description, license), so they are drop-in. But importing all 19 would duplicate what the house already has: mcp-builder against mcp-development, webapp-testing against sandbox-qa, claude-api against the house knowledge, internal-comms against the Telegram. The A/B picked the three the house really uses: pdf, doc-coauthoring and skill-creator. The pdf one would have arrived DEAD: its scripts need pdfplumber, pytesseract and pypdf, none of which were in the python of the house. Measured: without them 'import pdfplumber' failed; with all three in the devShell the skill's own scripts ran on a generated PDF and found the form field it was given. The write-up also corrects an over-optimistic claim of mine: the opencodeGo driver is the opencode CLOUD service (it wants an API key), not the local opencode of the house. The local bridge is the customAcp driver, whose 'cli' is the whole command, and the house opencode does speak ACP ('opencode acp'). What is proven and what is not is now in a table: the harness boots here and its API answers, the driver exists in the open source code, but a real conversational turn through it is still NOT proven, and it is listed as the next step instead of as a fait accompli. The section on the pains found on the way is in the same document.

feat(rag): the offline survival corpus as fallback of the online search The N.O.M.A.D corpus was exposed as a tool of the MCP but was wired to nothing: the web search answered a bare ERROR when Tavily was missing, and the semantic search never looked at the corpus. Two islands. Now the web search falls back to the corpus when the online one does not answer (no key, HTTP error, timeout, exception) and says so in the result (fonte: corpus offline N.O.M.A.D), because the corpus is local and deterministic (FTS5) and answering offline beats leaving the agent with nothing. The semantic search appends the corpus as ADDITIONAL data, marked offline/NOMAD, and if the corpus fails the semantic search is exactly as before: the offline is extra, never a dependency. Measured: with an invalid Tavily key the answer comes from the corpus with the source marked; the semantic search returns three code index hits plus the offline one; five new tests cover the fallback, the mark, the empty query and the case where the offline fails. The write-up also corrects the framing of the OpenMausBot: the UX of the house is the Mission Control (SvelteKit, still incomplete), so that project would be a tab of the Mission Control, not another app.

feat(renda): the real item on the screen becomes a label of the owner The practice bench only knew the twelve practice items written by hand. But the labels that pay are the fifty to a hundred qualification items the owner does in the browser, and there was no path at all for those to become labels. This closes that link. What it does: reads the text of the item (clipboard first, window OCR as the fallback), shows what it read so the owner can check it, takes the verdict and writes the label in the house schema. What it does not do: it does not click, does not submit and does not type into a third-party account. The owner keeps deciding and recording on the platform himself; only the label he already gave enters here. The screen OCR turned out to be fragile in field, measured: capturing the whole screen read 1919 characters with the terminal, the waybar and the other windows mixed in, and capturing the DeepSeek window read 525 characters of a different window entirely (SSH audit via Termix API), because grim -g cuts the screen region and not the window, so what shows up there is what is on top. The house already knows this (vision._prepare_window: focus plus opacity plus real fullscreen, because grim composites the stack). The capture uses that path, but the clipboard is the primary source: the owner selects the item and presses Ctrl+C, and the text arrives exact, with no recognition error, no wrong window and no competition with the rest of the screen. The label is the owner's: context is the text of the item as he saw it, answer is what he answered, never the key (the defect the practice bench had, fixed earlier today). Proven end to end: item on the clipboard, verdict 2, label written (id=cap-..., answer=2, source=uhrs-capture, no key in the context), then judgment-dataset.py turned it into a Laya item (type=choice, answer=MODERATELY, the four options) with no leakage.

docs(hub): the agent hub answers the whole LAN without a token, patch ready and proven The review the hub's own author asked for found two defects, both measured against the live service on :8091. The security one: the server listens on every interface (the code default is BIND '::' and the unit does not set BIND, so ss shows *:8091) and the iptables rule accepts 8091 from 0.0.0.0/0, meaning the whole LAN reaches it. No route checks any credential: measured, GET /api/transcript returns 200 with the transcript (tool inputs included, so file content in transit) and POST /api/wake returns 200 with nothing but a JSON body. The server uses the opencode password as a confused deputy, so anyone who reaches the port injects a user turn into any session of the fleet (including the red-team ones) and reads any transcript. The file's own header claims the token stays server side on loopback, but the bind is not loopback. The other one: the busy indicator was dead. The code read s.busy, and the session API does not have a busy field at all (the real keys are agent, cost, id, location, model, outcome, projectID, time, title, tokens), and the roster does not have one either, so busy was always zero and every agent rendered idle even while working, while the HTML still computed an elapsed time from that zero. The real source is time.updated. The fix is committed as a patch, not applied: the file has no claim in the roster, the lane that built it is live on another machine and the owner went to sleep, so the live file and the live service were left untouched. The patch adds a hub-specific token (AGENT_HUB_TOKEN or a 0600 token file, compared in constant time, failing closed when no token is configured), guards the two routes that leak or write, derives busy from time.updated with a 90 second window, caps the wake body at 64 KiB and changes the bind default to 127.0.0.1 (reaching the tailnet again becomes an explicit BIND=::, with the token still required). Proven on a temporary port with the live service untouched: 401 without a token on transcript and wake, 200 with it, listening only on loopback, and the busy flag now reading time.updated (the sweep agent showed busy, which it could never show before). The patch applies cleanly with patch -p0 and the result passes node --check.

docs(events): the SSE never receives the coord-mcp events, and the reason is structural The task was to post one heartbeat event from the coord-mcp and say whether the SSE received it. It did not, and the cause is measured rather than guessed. With the full MCP handshake on the coord-mcp (8765) and a coord_post status carrying a probe note, the MCP answered OK (the post went to the bus), while the SSE on 8090, opened during the post, emitted its init and its own colon heartbeat lines and zero lines from the coord-mcp. Publishing straight into the EventBus from a separate script did not arrive either, which rules out the payload and points at the transport. The EventBus is in-process. publish dispatches the handlers in that process's memory, the SSE only subscribes to the bus of its own process, and the coord code already publishes coord.post and coord.read into the bus of the coord-mcp process, which is a different one. The processes are four: the coord-mcp on 8765, the webui backend on 8090, a plain TCP forward on 8090 for the tailnet that pipes bytes without knowing about events, and the hub on 8091. So what is missing is a way for one process to publish into another's bus. The document records the three pieces of the fix: a POST /api/events route in the webui (that lane's file), the coord-mcp also posting to the webui fail-open so the bus never depends on the hub being up (this lane's file), and the hub consuming the SSE (the rest of task t-2). It also notes that the hub has no token on any interface today, so the security patch should be applied before the fleet events go out through the tailnet.

docs(redteam): the intrusion guard measured against its own evasion surface The Crouton asked whether the guard covers the text that enters the peer's session. Measured with the house guard itself: 12 of 16 test texts pass CLEAN, and the three conclusions are that the guard is Portuguese only (an intruder writing in English passes, which is the most likely case), that one extra word escapes (the vocabulary matches an exact phrase and the patterns match a literal form, so 'me' or 'your' in the middle is enough), and that the invisible and encoding surface is not covered at all (zero-width characters, hyphenation, letter spacing, leet and base64 all pass, because the fold lowercases and strips accents but removes nothing else). Also measured on the other side: the guard is fail-open in BOTH paths, so if the script is missing, broken or over the timeout the text goes in unfiltered and the peer is not told, and the plugin blocks the 'marcado' class that the bus deliberately lets through with a warning. The six fixes are ordered by cost, and the two that change behaviour are left as the owner's decision: failing closed may take the fleet down when the guard falls, and aligning the plugin to the bus changes a tool that was born yesterday.

feat(offline): the house proves it works without network, in one entrypoint Fleet queue item: check the local dependencies and test without network, through a single entrypoint. The house already had an offline corpus (N.O.M.A.D, Kiwix, FM 4-25.11, NHS: 18,943 docs in FTS5 under data/offline/corpus.db) and the web search falls back to it when the online search fails. But that offline works was an assertion: nobody checked the local dependencies, and no single command proved the operation without a network. scripts/house-offline.sh now does three things: it checks the local dependencies (the corpus and its document count, the FTS5 table, the Portuguese to English glossary, the shared jarvis environment file, the embedder, Qdrant and the Tavily key), it tests without network for real, and it proves the fallback. The test without network is real: unshare -n creates a network namespace with no route, so the process sees no interface, resolves no name and connects to nothing. Measured, the offline search answered in 0.07 to 0.13 seconds with the local source and license. The fallback proof is the one that matters: with the network cut, the online search fails against api.tavily.com and the answer comes from the local corpus, marked as offline. The survival branch depends on neither Tavily, nor the internet, nor an LLM. Three of my own checks were wrong and the first run said FTS5 unavailable because the check, not the corpus, was wrong: the FTS5 table is docs, since docs_idx is the internal index and does not take MATCH directly; the shared environment file lives in modules/ai/jarvis and not in src/jarvis; and the glossary keeps its pairs under entries. All corrected and re-measured. One trap worth keeping: without the shared jarvis environment, the web search fails with requests not installed, which looks like a missing network when it is a missing PYTHONPATH, so the fallback test uses the canonical environment. The script touches no other repository, does not touch the webui, installs nothing and calls no owner API. Measured state: ten dependency checks and two network-free tests pass, and the self-test passes five of five.

bench(voice): 35B-A3B expert-cache vs 8B denso on heldout3 — Codacus hypothesis refuted Backlog #08 (Lince). Measured quality + DUR on heldout3 (39 items, ck=v3): - 35B-A3B + LoRA duplex (unit llama-duplex-35b.service, --n-cpu-moe 44): 9/39 (23.1%), 61 s/token, 2.4 h/cycle. Gargalo: RAM/swap (31 GB total, 10+ GB swap used), experts page-in 358 GB read. - 4B MTP + LoRA v9 (production :8092): 29/39 (74.4%), 4.6-5.5 s/token, 3 min/cycle. 3 identical samples = determinism. - 8B denso (bonsai :8080, no voice LoRA): 0-1/39 (0-2.6%), 0.9 s/token. Fails: n_predict 6 cuts 'SILENCE' -> 'SILE', outputs 'thinking' not labels. Arm 35B SUBE (refuta '35B MoE impossivel' do bus), mas 15x mais lento e erra mais que o 4B MTP. A voz precisa sub-segundo: o classify_turn oficial (timeout 8 s) mede timeout, nao o modelo. Com timeout 180 s o 35B classifica (ex.: 'meu cao me mordeu' -> RESPOND, o 4B da SILENCE).
